quickSummary: Le Chatelier's principle states a system shifts to counteract applied changes. Adding inert gas at constant volume causes NO shift; at constant pressure, it shifts toward more gas moles. Catalysts speed attainment without altering K.

summaryBox.title: Le Chatelier's Principle
summaryBox.takeaway: If perturbed, equilibrium shifts to minimize the disturbance. Inert gas at const V: NO SHIFT. Catalyst: NO SHIFT.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
LE CHATELIER RESPONSE DECISION TREE
                                         │
     ┌──────────────────┬───────────────┼───────────────┬──────────────────┐
     ▼                  ▼               ▼               ▼                  ▼
CONCENTRATION       PRESSURE            TEMPERATURE     INERT GAS (Const V)INERT GAS (Const P)
├── Add Reactant ──►├── Increase $P$ ──►├── Increase $T$ ──► No Effect on      Volume increases ──►
│   Shift Right     │   Shifts to FEWER │   Shifts ENDO  │   Equilibrium!   Shifts to MORE
└── Remove Product ─┤   gaseous moles   └── Decrease $T$ ──► (Δn_g unchanged) gaseous moles
    Shift Right     └── Decrease $P$        Shifts EXO                     (Δn_g > 0).
conceptBreakdown.content: "If a chemical system at dynamic equilibrium is subjected to a change in concentration, temperature, pressure, or volume, the equilibrium shifts in a direction that counteracts/minimizes the applied perturbation."

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.2 Detailed Perturbation Matrix
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 Detailed Perturbation Matrix
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Increase [Reactant]**: Shifts **Forward (Right)** ($Q < K$). $K$ is unchanged.
• **Increase [Product]**: Shifts **Backward (Left)** ($Q > K$). $K$ is unchanged.
• **Increase Total Pressure ($P$)**: Shifts toward **fewer gaseous moles** ($\Delta n_g$). $K$ is unchanged.
• **Increase Temperature ($T$)**: Shifts in **Endothermic direction** ($\Delta H > 0$). **ALTERS $K$** ($K \uparrow$ for Endo, $K \downarrow$ for Exo).
• **Addition of Inert Gas (at Const $V$)**: **NO SHIFT** (partial pressures $P_i$ of reacting gases remain unchanged). $K$ is unchanged.
• **Addition of Inert Gas (at Const $P$)**: Shifts toward **greater gaseous moles** ($\Delta n_g > 0$) because total volume expands, lowering partial pressures. $K$ is unchanged.
• **Addition of Catalyst**: **NO SHIFT** (lowers $E_a$ equally for both forward and reverse paths). $K$ is unchanged.

quickRevision: Inert gas at const V: No shift in equilibrium position.
Inert gas at const P: Shifts toward side with more gas moles.
Increasing pressure shifts toward fewer gas moles.
Heating favors endothermic direction; cooling favors exothermic direction.
Only temperature can alter the numerical value of K.
